meetings.title: Kestrel Logistics: discovery call
segments: Grace, Ben, thanks for joining.
I'd love to spend most of this call understanding how you work today, and then Noah can show you anything that's relevant.
Grace, maybe start with your team?
Sure. Kestrel is a regional logistics company, about four hundred people.
I run operations, which includes our customer support team, about sixty people.
We deal with two kinds of customers, the shippers who pay us, and the people receiving deliveries, who don't pay us but definitely complain to us.
Ha. Where does the feedback come from today?
Everywhere. Support tickets in Zendesk, reviews of our driver and tracking apps, an NPS survey we send shippers every quarter, and a lot of notes our account managers write after calls.
Roughly how much feedback is that in a month?
Zendesk is around nine thousand tickets a month.
App reviews, maybe a few hundred.
NPS is quarterly, a couple of thousand responses each time.
And the account manager notes, honestly, no idea, they're scattered across people's documents.
The notes are usually the most valuable and the hardest to get at.
And what happens with it?

Honestly, that's the problem. Every week we have an operations review, and one of our analysts spends almost two full days pulling tickets and reviews into a spreadsheet so we can see what's going on.
By the time we see a trend, it's two weeks old.
Last spring we had a spike in complaints about missed delivery windows in one region.
It was right there in the tickets.
We didn't catch it for almost a month, and we lost one of our bigger shippers over it.
When you looked back at it, how early could you have seen it?
About three weeks earlier. The complaints started as a trickle in one region.
If someone had seen 'missed delivery window, northeast' growing week over week, we'd have added drivers.
Instead, we found out when the shipper's VP called our CEO.
That's painful. How big was that shipper, roughly?
Around four hundred thousand a year in revenue for us.
So it got the CEO's attention.
I can imagine.
What have you tried so far? Any tools?
We built a BI dashboard on top of Zendesk tags.
But the tags are inconsistent, every agent tags differently, so the dashboard is only as good as the tagging.
And it doesn't cover app reviews or NPS at all.
From the IT side, I'll add that we looked at one of the AI insights tools a couple of months ago.
The demo was impressive, but it's priced per seat, and we'd want most of the support team to have access. That got expensive fast.
What else did you like or dislike about their product, aside from price?
The demo was slick. But when we asked how it would handle our app reviews, they said it would need a custom connector, with a services fee.
That was the second red flag.
App store reviews are a standard connector for us. No services fee.
That's helpful to know. What would good look like, if you could wave a wand?
Monday morning, I open one screen and it tells me the top five things customers are unhappy about, whether they're getting worse, and I can click through to the actual tickets.
And I want my regional managers to see the same thing for their region.
How many regional managers would want access?
Six, one for each region.
Plus me, my director of support, and probably a couple of people in product.
So around a dozen people, but only a few of them every day.
Would the regional managers only see their own region, or everything?
Their own region by default, but able to look at others.
Operations is a team sport here.
That's a very typical shape.
A few daily users and a wider group checking in weekly.
That's very close to what we're building with our themes view.
It groups feedback from every source into themes, ranks them by volume and growth, and every theme links back to the underlying comments.
Let me show you a quick version on sample data.
Oh, that's exactly it. The growth arrows especially.
What do you need from us technically to set this up?
Do you need SSO or anything like that?
For a team your size, Google sign-in is usually enough.
Zendesk connects with an API token, and we can backfill ninety days of history.
App store reviews are just a public connector.
What about data security? Our shippers' names show up in tickets.
Where does the data live?
Everything is stored in the US, encrypted at rest and in transit.
For the AI features, text is processed by our model provider under an agreement that it isn't used for training or retained.
We can send you our security overview after the call.
That would be great. I'll need it for our vendor review, but it sounds standard.
Google sign-in is fine for us. That's easy.
Can I ask about budget and timing?
Is there a budget set aside for this?
Not formally. I think we could spend thirty to forty thousand a year if the value is clear.
Anything over twenty-five thousand needs our CFO to sign off, and he'll want to see numbers.
What numbers would your CFO want to see?
Time saved, for sure. The analyst's two days a week is easy to calculate.
But the real story is the shipper we lost.
If this catches one of those a year, it pays for itself many times over.
That's a strong case. I can help you put together a one page business case for him, if that's useful.
That would be very useful.
That's very reasonable. And timing?
I'd like something running by early next quarter, before our peak season.
That's when the complaints really spike.
One more thing. We're about to start an early access program for the new themes view, with a small group of customers.
It's free during the program, and you'd work closely with our product team.
Based on what you've described, you'd be a great fit.
What would you need from us as a design partner?
Mostly honest feedback, a short weekly check-in with our team, and real usage.
Our customer success lead would walk you through the details.
I'd be very interested in that.
Great. So, next steps from our side.
Noah will run a trial with your real Zendesk data so you can see your own themes.
I'll send a proposal, and I'll check with our product team about the early access program.
I'll set up a trial workspace with your Zendesk export by end of week.
What will you need from Ben to set that up? Just the API token?
Just the token with read access.
Ben, I'll send you the exact permissions so you can create it safely.
Perfect, that's easy.
And I'll send a proposal with pricing for the CFO conversation, and get back to you about early access.
Perfect. Thank you both, this is the most useful call I've had with a vendor this year.
